details: For all equal-size set-pairs with t-intersecting A-family and cross-intersections, source Conjecture 4.1 asks AK(a+b,a,t). Its concluding paragraph explicitly reports Scott–Wilmer's proof using interior products. Source Theorem 1.5 has stronger cross-t hypotheses and is not itself a bridge. No investment; external proof body not fetched or independently audited.

Every odd p and every effective locally linear homologically trivial action on a closed orientable four-manifold of nonzero Euler characteristic. Remark 1.1 supplies the fixed-point case; nonzero Euler characteristic alone is not a global-fixed-point argument. Spectral-sequence/topological obstruction remains; no small admissible action survives as concrete counterexample route.

Equality of classes requires both implications for all compact metric spaces and every real p>1. Source Proposition 3.25 proves the forward inclusion using connected closed one-dimensional subsets; arbitrary compact spaces with all snowflake quotients trivial are the missing direction. Finite spaces cannot settle that direction; no concrete pathological compact construction qualified.

For every parameter pair in I times Omega the specified point must be the unique GLOBAL nearest point. Source Conjecture 6.4 and local-minimum context distinguish this from Theorem 6.6, which assumes the conjectural uniqueness. A semialgebraic certificate over the full two-parameter domain is needed, not local Hessians or sampled minimizers; exact boundary/dependency and successor qualification incomplete.

All subcubic graphs require a proper edge coloring with six colors and no bichromatic four-edge path/cycle. Source Conjecture 1.1 records seven-color and special-family bounds. A universal reduction/extension argument is absent; small satisfiable instances cannot prove the assertion and no concrete certified obstruction is available.

All finite groups, D(G) means relative subgroup commutativity degrees, not ordinary single-group commuting probability. Source Conjecture 1.4 and Theorem 1.5 separate the general chain-length lower bound from classification when exactly five values occur. Enumerating a few small groups would not bridge arbitrary central quotients; no tractable family with an exact failure was identified.

Huang arXiv1907.00847v2 Theorem 1.5 gives bs(f)<=s(f)^4 for every Boolean f, exactly the required absolute exponent C=4. Read all six pages, including recursive signed-cube matrix proof, interlacing, degree bridge and references. Gotsman–Linial and Tal results are cited dependencies, not independently replayed here. The database's own statement already says solved.

Every admissible t congruent to 0,1,2 mod6 and every r>floor(t/6), over ALL fields. Source Conjecture 7.1 separates the symmetric ECG(6q+1,6q+1) theorem from general unequal parameters. Finite-field rank tests cannot prove universal field-optimality; graph-domain and zero-forcing transfer for asymmetric cases remain unqualified.

Historical r304 exclusion is confirmed by fresh primary successor Battistoni–Molteni2211.16842 Theorem1, sharp P5,1<=16M=16.6965..., and Section5, including the exact maximizing tuple from the old restricted Q. The restricted configuration lies within the successor's global ordered-root domain; published equality attains it. No new credit; lengthy polynomial certificates/dependencies not independently replayed.

All n>=4, both parity patterns and exact threshold C(1)=4. The same successor discusses iterative conjecture and proves low-degree cases, not an all-n maximizer theorem in the passages read. An isolated n=5 case cannot resolve this universal claim, and no uniform factorization/dominance induction was qualified.

For every divisor satisfying the source's special freeness/comparison hypotheses, all filtration steps l>=0 must be generated at the prescribed Bernstein–Sato level. Selected introduction discusses root multiplicities and Conjecture4.12; exact hypothesis list and D-module dependencies not fully audited. A computed divisor example or lower generation level alone is insufficient to refute an upper generation bound.

For each k>=2, finiteness over graphs with variable maximum degree requires the paper's graph conventions and f(k,Delta), not only a fixed-Delta theorem. Source Theorem7 only proves finiteness with gap<k-2 and Delta>=3. Low-degree/disconnected literal loopholes are scope corrections, not credit. No full universal sparing-k route qualified.

For each fixed m>=2, all sufficiently large geometric distance-regular graphs with diameter>=3 AND mu>=2 must be one of four families. Source Conjecture1.7 contains mu>=2, only in the database's explanatory paragraph. Theorems characterizing special Johnson/Hamming cases do not cover all intersection arrays; omitted-hypothesis variants earn no credit.

Existence of gamma0 followed by every sufficiently small positive gamma requires a sharp density LOWER bound for arbitrary tower configurations, not just the displayed lattice upper construction. Source Conjecture12 and the lattice determinant computation make this distinction explicit. Nonpositive-gamma wording and scaling corrections are uncredited; no global discharging certificate qualified.

One absolute c must work simultaneously for every regular degree d and order n, with total vertex/edge labels in [k] and all vertex products distinct. Source Conjecture6.3 is stronger than separate degree-dependent bounds. A local-lemma route would need anti-concentration uniform in d with shared edge variables; no such full-scope estimate established. Trivial n=1/log endpoint is a domain defect, not discovery.

Uniform coefficient-of-variation bound over all finite weighted graph metrics and uniform starting vertices. Source Conjecture5 modifies the maximum/minimum question and discusses exponential random edge lengths separately. Tie-breaking/connectedness conventions matter; one anomalous start does not yield large variance without sufficient probability. No scalable metric family with proved NUV trajectories qualified.

Source itself states Theorem2 for every integer k>=2 and every graph G, exactly tau_k^*<=2nu. Charging proofs for denominator3 and denominator2 are followed by combination to general k; selected construction/analysis passages read. No new argument warranted; long case-analysis appendices and all structural lemmas not independently audited.

Every nonconstant monotone coordinate-transitive Boolean function, with exact D(f)=n. Source proves almost-all monotone evasiveness in its random-complex setting, which does not imply every transitive function. Topological non-collapsibility/decision-tree lower bounds remain; a finite table would only cover instances.

For every n exists C_n uniform in positive measure and delta>0. Source Conjectures4.22/4.24 and conditional Lemma4.23 distinguish proved n<=3 from arbitrary products of trees. Substituting kappa=1/n presupposes the missing surrogate maximum principle; no valid dimension induction or exact positive-measure failure established.

All graphs under the actual strong coloring partition/transversal definition. The database's neighborhood-clique description is not that definition. Source Conjecture1.5 and partial ISR results do not prove the all-Delta bound; Delta=0 and literal gloss counterexamples earn no credit. No full strong-coloring mechanism qualified.

All alpha and every epsilon with normalized rho log n coding rates require the genuine increasing-power Poisson channel definition. The cited arXiv2001.06311 retained body concerns DNA noisy shuffling/sampling capacity, not the displayed PCIP conjecture in the inspected theorem sections. Wrong-source correction is uncredited; no capacity proof or primary scope qualification claimed.

Every degree4 maximal arc in PG(2,2^m), m>=2, requires both minimum weight4 and classification of every weight4 word as a block row. Source Conjecture3.1 separates Desarguesian arcs from extra minimum words in other order16 planes. Those other-plane examples are inadmissible counterexamples. No all-m incidence-code rigidity proof qualified.

Every digraph/order/W partition with all prescribed n_i>=3 and semidegree>=2n/3. The source explains this would imply disjoint directed triangle-factor conjectures. Its sharpness example lies below threshold; transplanting it is invalid. No above-threshold obstruction or universal prescribed-intersection cycle decomposition obtained.

Minimum over ALL 3-polytopes and generic functionals equals floor((n+5)/4), every n>=4. Source Conjecture6.1 distinguishes extremal simple-polytope attainment at even n from a universal diameter lower bound. Computing a few oriented polytopes cannot prove the min bound; no concrete lower-diameter candidate or full reduction qualified.

Every integer pair n/3<s<=n/2 with minimum over ALL k>=1, not only local critical-ratio intervals. Source Theorems1.2/1.3 prove near-threshold or high-minimum-degree cases. Blow-up constructions give candidate lower bounds but no general extremal upper bound; no integer-rounding failure established.

Every optimal dimension4 binary code at arbitrary length must admit extension to an optimal self-orthogonal code, with exact extension conventions. Source ConjectureV.13 follows finite examples and dimension-specific theorems. A reduction via 15 nonzero column multiplicities would need exact periodicity and extension-length constraints; these and closest successor proof bodies remain unqualified.

One rho must give strict monotonicity on three entire intervals, including an infinite tail. Source Conjecture6.3 follows only a local-maximum proposition. This beta depends on the paper's number-theoretic definitions, not an elementary beta distribution; no global derivative sign bound or rigorous tail certificate qualified.

For each Delta>=3, two-sided asymptotic threshold for bounded-degree H-factor games requires uniform embedding strategy, not a single clique-factor construction. Source Conjecture1.3 explicitly separates these settings. Divisibility/game conventions and constants do not supply an asymptotic refutation; no universal Maker strategy qualified.

All finite forbidden families F and target graphs H, asymptotically in n. Source Conjecture2.6 has unrestricted wording, but F containing H or a nonplanar H gives identically zero counts, requiring a nonzero-case convention for Theta(n^k). Such domain corrections earn no credit. Theorem2.7 for trees with forbidden even cycles does not prove the arbitrary nonzero-case statement.

All planar graphs in each of three independent universal induced-degeneracy ratios. Source Theorem1.1 gives 3/4 for d=3 while Conjecture1.1 asks 5/6; octahedron/icosahedron upper examples do not prove lower bounds. No finite extremal obstruction beyond known witnesses or uniform discharging theorem obtained.

Every positive k,s and d>=2s require exact k-fold chromatic equality. Source Conjecture1.3 lists known k=1, divisibility and small-s cases. LP fractional chromatic number alone loses the integrality ceiling; no all-parameter lower certificate or admissible coloring below the asserted formula qualified. Nonpositive integer loopholes are outside intended coloring domain.

Every formal 2-function W, with its spectral curve and all genus terms, must satisfy quantum2 integrality. Source Conjecture3.6 is a converse construction, not a consequence of taking the classical limit. Spectral-curve admissibility and recursion-to-integrality dependencies are unqualified; checking finitely many coefficients would not prove all W/all orders.

D-finiteness/nonalgebraicity concerns the generic two-variable series D(s,z); special s=1 recovers algebraic Catalan enumeration and is not a new refutation. Source Conjecture6.2 specifies fifth order, degree27, after the walk equation. A guessed annihilator plus finite coefficients does not certify the functional-equation solution; no exact creative-telescoping/nonalgebraicity proof qualified.

For each maximum vertex incidence Delta there must exist a finite label bound uniform in number AND sizes of hyperedges. Source Conjecture14 records Delta=2 as already known and leaves Delta=3. Pairwise constraints share unbounded supports; a naive dependency-degree LLL bound is not uniform. Identical-set self-comparison is a wording issue. No concrete obstruction or uniform decorrelation construction qualified.

For EVERY k>=3 requires a connected path-factor graph of exact degree k with non-Hamiltonian P_(4k-4) product. Source Conjecture6.1 follows nearby sufficient conditions, so degree gadgets must preserve both the path factor and obstruction. Bipartite imbalance alone vanishes because the path has even order. No scalable cut/toughness certificate survived qualification.

For each finite poset P, bounded induced saturation versus >=n+1 for EVERY n. Source nonseparation/blowing-up argument proves only logarithmic lower bound from a separating family. Replacing log n by n+1 is not an algebraic strengthening; needs additional saturation structure. Small-n certificates cannot settle the unbounded alternative; no route qualified.

All path orders n>=3 and cycle orders n>=5, using slides among maximum irredundant sets with private-neighbor conditions. Source survey Conjecture4.1 concerns this exact reconfiguration object. It is not a generic independent-set slide graph. Known short exclusions do not force all larger paths/cycles; no structural endpoint argument established.

Source already claims complete resolution and gives Theorem2.2 rank(S+5I)>=floor(2N/3)+1 for N>=277. Proposition2.1 supplies the equiangular-line/Seidel bridge and later sections finish its proof. Selected theorem/concluding proof passages read, not all forbidden-subgraph lemmas. No discovery investment; underlying exhaustive dependencies not independently replayed.

All n,k for vincular underlined23-14 avoidance and right-to-left minima. Source Conjecture4.1 explicitly relates this to zero counts in inversion sequences; its invcode Proposition3.5 concerns a DIFFERENT vincular class and does not supply the desired bijection. Exact enumeration n<=8 matches recurrence but gives no universal proof. Closest later enumerative theorem/proof bodies and current registry remain unqualified; no brief.

For each fixed uniformity k and H exists a constant in O(n^(k-1)). Source Conjecture5.7 names the missing hypergraph analogue of its graph tree lemma. Ordinary saturation bounds do not automatically survive proper rainbow coloring constraints. No explicit universal saturated construction or super-polynomial exact obstruction qualified.

For every surface and n, EVERY total-clique maximizer must simultaneously maximize each s-clique count. Source Conjecture6.11 is stronger in equality cases than aggregate Conjecture6.10. Triangulating or maximizing edges does not force triangles and higher cliques simultaneously on arbitrary genus; no exact surface-enumeration counterexample certified.

Every bounded-degree tree of asymptotically (1-o(1))*2log_q(np) vertices throughout C(Delta)/n<p<0.99. Source Conjecture1 separates the sparse gap from dense-range theorems. The database reference about size of a largest induced tree is weaker than embedding EVERY prescribed tree. No sparse second-moment/universal embedding bridge qualified.

All positive a,n and every union-closed family with element frequencies<=a, cardinality<=2a. Source Conjecture0.3 explicitly states equivalence with Frankl. Linear relaxations and small-ground-set checks are not the integer universal bound; no concrete tight-family induction or admissible refutation available.

Asymptotic Theta(n^2) for the specified Pref-opposite construction, but the source defines discrepancy over all CYCLIC SUBSTRINGS, whereas the database defines maximum prefix imbalance. These differ in exact value and are comparable up to factor2 for a balanced full cycle, so wording is not an asymptotic refutation. Source Conjecture3.2 and empirical suffix are not an all-n suffix proof; no uniform analysis qualified.

Exact binomial formula and global maximality for every order n require the paper's cyclic-substring discrepancy, not the record's prefix definition. Source Section5 gives DBmax construction and lower bound via weight-range cycles, not the exact global upper theorem. Definition correction or finite rotation examples earn no credit; universal extremal upper bound unqualified.

Every B2 dumbbell graph of order n>=11, with exact equality classification. Both retained unversioned and explicit v1 primary bodies define B2(p,l,q), n=p+q+l-1, but their concluding conjecture concerns a larger bicyclic family with different parity-dependent B3 extremizers; the literal B2 target was not located in those inspected sections. Need exact source/version before solving radical inequalities or promoting a finite dumbbell sweep.

Source Theorem1.4 explicitly disproves Conjecture1.3. Self-complementarity gives summed coefficient 2*(23/164)=23/82, strictly exceeding 7/25 by 1/2050 along infinitely many n. Read Section3.1 construction, clique-partition lemma/proof and leading-term optimization. This complete explicit bridge is already public, with construction/dependency lemmas not independently replayed; zero credit.

Every dimension and EVERY finite-dimensional real norm, not only polyhedral norms of small codimension. Source Conjecture1 and its codimension/facet corollaries leave large-codimension cases. Arbitrary simplex Euclidean constructions do not preserve equal norm distances under arbitrary norms; no universal extension argument qualified.

Exists ONE fixed d, then for every bound C a d-regular Cayley graph with no orthonormal C-bounded eigenbasis, using normalized L2. Source Conjecture1.5 distinguishes growing-degree constructions and bounded irreducible-dimension positive cases. A single badly localized eigenvector does not exclude a different basis in a repeated eigenspace. No fixed-generator representation family with basis-independent obstruction qualified.

Every subcubic graph, subdivision once, five packing colors with distance>=i+1 in class i. Source Conjecture1 and Proposition2 supply a transformation from S-colorings but known subcubic S-colorings yield weaker palettes. Outerplanar subclasses do not cover all graphs; no universal five-color reduction or exact unsatisfiable subdivision certificate qualified.
